observations: A rounded head shape sits centered on a white oval ground, built from overlapping scribbled lines in teal, orange, red, black, and white, with eyes rendered as two horizontal dark bands beneath a dense crosshatched forehead.

The mouth area shows a visible row of white teeth and a red-lined interior opening; the lower jaw dissolves into loose trailing marks against the white ground, giving the bottom of the face an unfinished, open quality.
Concentric wavy bands of green, yellow, and white frame the composition, with the outer corners filled by loose magenta, red, and teal scribbles that do not touch the central oval.
reading: The mouth opening dominates the lower half, pulling attention downward while dense crosshatching above holds the forehead closed and heavy. That contrast—compressed marks at the top, an open void below—reads as tension between containment and release. The concentric framing bands push the head forward rather than receding, so the face feels pressed toward the viewer. Color layering is cool-dominant at the center and warm at the edges, reversing the expected figure-ground relationship.
contextAngle: Within the owned nifty-faces subset, this work sits between #7 and #9 in both title order and recorded creation order. Where #7 fills the field with saturated red, this work introduces a white oval ground that isolates the head—a structural choice absent in either immediate neighbor.

connections.reason: Both works show a visible tooth row as a focal anchor in the lower face, but #7 fills the entire field with red and uses square-framed eye sockets, while #8 floats the head on white with concentric oval bands—a direct contrast in how the face is grounded.

Scrimshaw13 shares the collector-noted visual link: both use layered multicolor scribble lines to build a frontal head on a light ground, with circular eye marks and a visible tooth row, making the cross-collection formal parallel concrete.

lookingQuestion: Where exactly does the dense crosshatching stop and the open white ground begin—and does that boundary hold consistently around the whole head?
ambiguities: The signature in the lower right reads as 'NVI xyz 29' or similar; the numeral is legible as content but its meaning is unverified.
